answers.question: The rule on handing a case to staff says more than your later answers. Before: "The agent hands the case to staff when a cancel or refund call fails or gets no answer, or the refund differs from what the customer confirmed, and tells the customer that staff will follow up. When the follow-up call gets no answer it sends it once more; if that gets no answer too, it tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support." After: "The agent hands the case to staff when it cannot finish: when a refund call fails, when what a cancel or refund call did is still unknown or not done after the reads and the one more call the other rules allow, or when the refund differs from what the customer confirmed; and it tells the customer that staff will follow up. When the follow-up call gets no answer it sends it once more; if that gets no answer too, it tells the customer to contact Harbor Goods support." Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule to the "after" text.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process.
> Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.

answers.question: The rule on refund retries hands the case to staff at once after a final error, even when the first refund call got no answer and you said the agent then retries once and re-reads. Before: "The agent sends the refund call a second time only after a temporary error or no answer, and never a third time. After a final error it sends no second call: it hands the case to staff and tells the customer the refund was not issued, without claiming success." After: "The agent sends the refund call a second time only after a temporary error or no answer, and never a third time. After a final error on the first call it sends no second call: it hands the case to staff and tells the customer the refund was not issued, without claiming success. When the first call got no answer, the agent reads the order and its refund again after the second call, whatever that call answers, unless it answers a refund for a different amount." Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule to the "after" text.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process.
> One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
> Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds.
> Final message must match the final refund status.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.

answers.question: Nothing says what the agent does when a customer asks to cancel more than one order. Before: "When the customer has more than one open order and does not say which, the agent asks which one. The proposal always names the order number, and no cancel call comes before the customer confirms it." After: the same, plus "When the customer asks to cancel more than one order, in one message or one after another, the agent takes them one at a time: each order gets its own proposal and its own yes, and a yes to one order does not cover another." Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule to the "after" text.

answers.question: After the second cancel call also gets no answer and the order still shows placed or processing, the agent hands the case to staff. None of the follow-up call's four reasons (refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown, refund amount differs) says the order is still open, so staff would get "cancellation unknown" for an order known not to be cancelled. What reason does the agent send?
answers.recommended: Add a fifth reason, "order not cancelled", and send it in that case.
